tagline: Providing reliable, high-quality water service to communities across California, New Mexico, Hawaii, and Texas
hero_kpi_rationale: CWT's business model is entirely dependent on regulatory approval of costs and investments through public commissions. The ability to recover regulatory assets (such as water costs, infrastructure, or TCJA) is the primary driver of its financial trajectory, far more than organic growth or technological innovation.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Net income attributable to the company after taxes and expenses.
kpis.description: Net income declined by 33.8% in 2025 to $128.2M, compared to $190.8M in 2024, primarily due to the absence of the one-time gain related to the 2021 GRC and higher operating costs.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in 2025 following a 2024 peak linked to rate adjustments

kpis.name: Operating Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from water sales and related services.
kpis.description: Operating revenue was $1,000.1M in 2025, down $36.7M (-3.5%) from 2024 ($1,036.8M), primarily due to lower consumption (-$12.7M), partially offset by higher rates (+$69.6M).
kpis.signal: Revenue impacted by rate regulation and customer consumption

kpis.name: Operating Expenses
kpis.explanation: Costs related to water production, operations, and general overhead.
kpis.description: Total operating expenses increased by $18.0M in 2025, driven by water production costs (+$11.5M), depreciation expenses (+$12.5M), and property taxes (+$3.7M).
kpis.signal: Significant increase in operating costs in 2025

kpis.name: Water Production Costs
kpis.explanation: Costs of purchased water, electricity, and pumping taxes, representing the largest component of operating expenses.
kpis.description: Total water production costs (purchased water + purchased electricity + pumping taxes) increased in 2025. Purchased water rose from $241.2M to $252.9M (+$11.7M or +4.9%), while purchased electricity decreased from $47.7M to $45.1M (-$2.6M or -5.5%).
kpis.signal: Growing pressure on water production costs

kpis.name: Depreciation
kpis.explanation: Spreading infrastructure investment costs over multiple years.
kpis.description: Depreciation expenses increased by $12.5M in 2025, reflecting continued investment in water distribution infrastructure.

kpis.name: Interest Expense
kpis.explanation: Cost of financing the company's debt.
kpis.description: Net interest expenses increased by $9.1M in 2025 due to higher borrowing levels, even though interest rates declined.
kpis.signal: Rising interest expenses despite lower rates

kpis.name: TCJA Liability
kpis.explanation: Amount owed related to the 2017 U.S. tax reform, to be recovered through rates.
kpis.description: The liability related to the TCJA tax reform amounted to $60.6M as of December 31, 2025. The company is working with regulators to finalize its recovery through rates.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of $5.67B in the latest year

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Net income attributable to the company after taxes and expenses.
kpis.description: Net income declined by 33.8% in 2025 to $128.2M, compared to $190.8M in 2024, due to the absence of the one-time gain related to the 2021 GRC.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in 2025 following a 2024 peak

kpis.name: Regulatory Asset Recovery
kpis.explanation: The company's ability to recover its costs through rates approved by commissions, illustrated by the 2021 GRC gain.
kpis.description: 2024 net income includes a $64.0M gain related to the 2021 GRC (or $1.09 per diluted share), reflecting the recovery of operating and investment costs through rates. This amount represents the benefit of a retroactive temporary rate relief effective January 1, 2023.
kpis.signal: $64M gain related to 2021 GRC included in 2024

risks.title: Regulation
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to strict regulations and changes in laws or regulator policies can have a significant impact on its business. Decisions by Commissions are outside its control and may affect its revenues and financial results.

risks.title: Regulated Rates
risks.score_rationale: The rates the company charges its customers are subject to approval by Commissions, which may affect its revenues and financial results. Commission decisions may be delayed or approved at a lower level than requested.

risks.title: Water Quality
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to strict water quality standards and changes in regulations may increase its operating costs. Test results indicating water exceeds allowable limits may require costly treatment.

risks.title: Climate Change
risks.score_rationale: The company may be affected by changes in laws and regulations related to climate change, which may increase its operating costs and affect its financial results.

risks.title: Cybersecurity
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to cybersecurity risks, including attacks on its systems and data, which may affect its operations and financial results.

risks.title: Reputation
risks.score_rationale: The company may be affected by reputational issues, including non-compliance with water quality or safety standards, which may affect its financial results and operations.

ai_positioning.summary: The company CWT has no significant mentions regarding artificial intelligence or machine learning in the provided excerpts.
